title: Reinstate the two-child limit in universal credit
headline: Bring back the two-child limit. Saves £3.1bn in 2029-30.
description: Budget 2025 removed the limit on the universal credit child element for third and subsequent children from April 2026. Switch this on to bring the limit back from April 2027, saving the Treasury's costing of the removal (£3.1bn in 2029-30). The scorecard title says the removal takes 450,000 children out of poverty.

baselinePolicy.text: Two-child limit removed from April 2026 at a cost rising from £2.4bn in 2026-27 to £3.2bn in 2030-31 (Budget 2025, Table 4.1 line 6).
alreadyIncludes: Removal of the two-child limit on the universal credit child element from April 2026 (Budget 2025, Table 4.1 line 6).

lines.title: Universal Credit Child Element: Remove the two child limit from April 2026, taking 450,000 children out of poverty

rawSource.note: Reversal on the spending side: the Treasury's costing with the sign kept (a measure that increased borrowing was more spending; reversing it is the same amount of spending saved).

caveats: The Treasury's costing is on the OBR November 2025 forecast, not the March 2026 baseline used here; the difference is small relative to the figures. Effects before the start year are not applied.

considerations.text: The Treasury's static cost of removing the limit (£2.7bn in 2029-30) rises to £3.1bn after a take-up response: 11% of newly entitled and 22% of previously entitled but non-claiming households are assumed to start claiming, which the Treasury calls uncertain. Reinstating the limit is assumed here to save the full post-behavioural figure.
The Treasury's scorecard describes the removal as taking 450,000 children out of poverty; reinstating the limit would reverse that, concentrated on larger low-income families.

The Treasury's scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; see the Budget 2025 policy costings document for the method.
